title: No integer squares to minus one
statement: There is no integer x with x * x = -1.

provenance.source: authored by the skolem-cert lane as the replacement negative control for scripts/check-smt-evidence-certified.py; statement written here, not copied

notes:
OPEN IN THIS LEDGER, NOT IN MATHEMATICS, and open for exactly one reason: axeyum gets the right VERDICT and attaches no checkable object. Measured 2026-08-17 with `./target/release/examples/smtcomp_cli --evidence artifacts/facts/smt2/neg-no-integer-square-is-minus-one.smt2`: `; evidence kind=unsat-uncertified certified=0 recheck=na arena=none:uncertified-unsat ms=0`, then `unsat`. An uncertified unsat is not evidence under this schema, so the status stays `open`.

THIS INSTANCE IS THE NEGATIVE CONTROL of `scripts/check-smt-evidence-certified.py`. That check requires every settled smt-term-level / smt-clausal fact to report `certified=1`, and it needs one case where it can demonstrate it would notice `certified=0` -- otherwise a check that only ever confirms health cannot show it can see illness. The control must be genuinely unsat (so the ledger's usual verdict-only command shape passes it) and genuinely uncertified (so a certification-aware check must not). This one is both, and it is cheap: 0 ms, so it costs the gate nothing.

It took this role on 2026-08-17 from `artifacts/facts/smt2/neg-barber-no-such-barber.smt2`, which had held it since the check was written and stopped discriminating the same day: the `skolem-cert` lane made a skolemised refutation certify, the barber began reporting `kind=unsat-quant-instance-set certified=1 arena=ok`, the control failed ON PURPOSE with the message it was written to emit, and `F:barber-no-such-barber` was closed. That is the intended life cycle of this fact too. If it ever reports `certified=1`, that check FAILS on purpose, saying this fact can now be closed and the control must be repointed again.

WHY IT IS UNCERTIFIED, as far as measured: the refutation is a `QF_NIA` sign argument (a square is non-negative, so it cannot equal -1) reached after the exact integer refuters decline, and it lands on the bare `Evidence::Unsat(None)` fallback. Certifying it needs a nonlinear-sign certificate over the integers -- the `unsat-sos` route already certifies the REAL analogue (`(assert (< (* x x) 0.0))` in QF_NRA reports `kind=unsat-sos certified=1 arena=ok`, measured the same day), so the gap is the integer route, not the mathematics.
